body.p: The Git Branch Manager view shows the local and remote branches for the current repository. By default, it opens to the right of the editing area. You can open it in any of the following ways:

ul.li: Click Show Git Branch Manager in the toolbar of the Git Staging view.
Go to Window Show View Git Branch Manager .

section.title: Main Areas
section.p: The main areas in the Git Branch Manager view are:

ul.li: Text filter - Filters the branch tree.
Refresh - Reloads branch information for the current repository. Opening the view or clicking Refresh also fetches updates in the background so remote branches and tracking information stay current.
Repository tree - Shows the current repository and groups its branches into Local and Remote nodes.

section.title: Branch Tree
section.p: Use the branch tree to inspect local and remote branches. When you hover over a branch name, a tooltip shows information about the last commit on that branch, such as the author and commit date.
For remote branches, use Checkout branch to create a local branch from the selected remote branch.

The context menu for the remote branch area also provides fetch actions. Right-click Remote to fetch all configured remotes, or right-click an individual remote such as origin to fetch only that remote.

section.title: Local Branch Actions
section.p: The context menu for each local branch includes the following actions:

fig.title: Git Branch Manager Local Branch Context Menu

ul.li:
Pull - displays either Pull (merge) or Pull (rebase) based on your choice in the Git Staging Pull dropdown.
Pull (merge) - Pulls remote changes and merges them into the current branch.
Pull (rebase) - Pulls remote changes and rebases local unpublished commits on top of them.
Push - Sends local commits from the current branch to the remote repository. Pull and Push actions are disabled for branches without a tracked remote.
Checkout - Switches to the selected branch.

p.note: If unpulled changes are detected when you create a branch, a confirmation dialog box lets you choose whether to pull the changes before the branch is created.
To publish a new branch to the remote repository and start tracking that branch, push the local branch from the Git Staging view.

ul.li: Track remote branch - Sets the remote branch used for fetch, pull, and push.
Merge "SELECTED_BRANCH" into "CURRENT_BRANCH" - Merges the selected branch into the current branch.
Squash merge "SELECTED_BRANCH" into "CURRENT_BRANCH" - Combines the branch changes into one commit.
Show in history - Selects the branch head in history.
